description: Guidewire login history, backed by SQL Server so it is not capped by Loki's ~30-day retention. Fed daily by the GW-Login-Collector pipeline.

panels.title: Total logins
panels.description: Login events in the selected range. One user logging in 5x counts 5.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ISNULL(SUM(logins), 0) AS "Total logins"
FROM [${db}].dbo.gw_login_daily
WHERE $__timeFilter(day_ts)
    AND project IN (${project:sqlstring})
    AND env IN (${env:sqlstring})
    AND product IN (${product:sqlstring});

panels.title: Distinct users
panels.description: TRUE distinct users across the whole range -- counted from stored usernames, not by summing daily figures (which would count anyone active on several days more than once). A figure daily counts alone cannot give.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT username) AS "Distinct users"
FROM [${db}].dbo.gw_login_user_daily
WHERE $__timeFilter(day_ts)
    AND username <> '(unparsed)'
    AND project IN (${project:sqlstring})
    AND env IN (${env:sqlstring})
    AND product IN (${product:sqlstring});

panels.title: Collector lag
panels.description: Days between today and the most recent day with data, for the most-behind selected project. Each project is measured by its freshest environment, so a decommissioned environment does not hold this red. 1 is normal. 3+ means investigate NOW: once a gap passes Loki's ~30-day retention it is unrecoverable. Ignores the dashboard time range and the Environment/Product filters on purpose.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ISNULL(MAX(lag), 9999) AS "Days behind"
FROM (SELECT project, MIN(days_behind) AS lag
      FROM [${db}].dbo.gw_login_freshness
      WHERE project IN (${project:sqlstring})
      GROUP BY project) x;

SELECT project + ' / ' + env AS env, SUM(logins) AS logins
FROM [${db}].dbo.gw_login_daily
WHERE $__timeFilter(day_ts)
    AND project IN (${project:sqlstring})
    AND env IN (${env:sqlstring})
    AND product IN (${product:sqlstring})
GROUP BY project, env
ORDER BY SUM(logins) DESC;

panels.title: Daily logins by environment
panels.description: From SQL Server, not Loki -- so this reaches back as far as the collector has run, not 30 days.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT day_ts AS time, project + ' / ' + env AS metric, SUM(logins) AS value
FROM [${db}].dbo.gw_login_daily
WHERE $__timeFilter(day_ts)
    AND project IN (${project:sqlstring})
    AND env IN (${env:sqlstring})
    AND product IN (${product:sqlstring})
GROUP BY day_ts, project, env
ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Daily distinct users by environment
panels.description: Unique users PER DAY. These cannot be added up across days -- for a true range-wide figure see the 'Distinct users' stat, which counts usernames.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT day_ts AS time, project + ' / ' + env AS metric, SUM(distinct_users) AS value
FROM [${db}].dbo.gw_login_daily
WHERE $__timeFilter(day_ts)
    AND project IN (${project:sqlstring})
    AND env IN (${env:sqlstring})
    AND product IN (${product:sqlstring})
GROUP BY day_ts, project, env
ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Monthly logins by environment
panels.description: Logins per calendar month. Edge months in the selected range are partial.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
    CAST(DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR([day]), MONTH([day]), 1) AS DATETIME2(0)) AS time,
    project + ' / ' + env AS metric,
    SUM(logins) AS value
FROM [${db}].dbo.gw_login_daily
WHERE $__timeFilter(day_ts)
    AND project IN (${project:sqlstring})
    AND env IN (${env:sqlstring})
    AND product IN (${product:sqlstring})
GROUP BY DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR([day]), MONTH([day]), 1), project, env
ORDER BY 1;

SELECT
    d.project                                        AS [Project],
    d.env                                            AS [Environment],
    d.product                                        AS [Product],
    SUM(d.logins)                                    AS [Logins],
    COUNT(*)                                         AS [Days with data],
    CAST(ROUND(AVG(CAST(d.logins AS FLOAT)), 0) AS INT) AS [Avg per day],
    MAX(d.logins)                                    AS [Peak day],
    MAX(d.[day])                                     AS [Last day]
FROM [${db}].dbo.gw_login_daily d
WHERE $__timeFilter(d.day_ts)
    AND d.project IN (${project:sqlstring})
    AND d.env IN (${env:sqlstring})
    AND d.product IN (${product:sqlstring})
GROUP BY d.project, d.env, d.product
ORDER BY d.project, d.env, d.product;

panels.title: Most active users
panels.description: Only possible because usernames are stored per day. Environments are counted per project (DEV1 in two projects counts 2). Note this table holds user identifiers -- treat access accordingly.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT TOP 25
    username      AS [User],
    SUM(logins)   AS [Logins],
    COUNT(DISTINCT [day])   AS [Active days],
    COUNT(DISTINCT project) AS [Projects],
    COUNT(DISTINCT project + '/' + env) AS [Environments]
FROM [${db}].dbo.gw_login_user_daily
WHERE $__timeFilter(day_ts)
    AND username <> '(unparsed)'
    AND project IN (${project:sqlstring})
    AND env IN (${env:sqlstring})
    AND product IN (${product:sqlstring})
GROUP BY username
ORDER BY SUM(logins) DESC;

panels.title: Collector runs (most recent 20)
panels.description: Health of the pipeline feeding this dashboard, one row per project per run. 'partial' means some Loki queries failed and those cells kept their previous values; the next run's lookback retries them.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT TOP 20
    started_at   AS [Started (UTC)],
    project      AS [Project],
    status       AS [Status],
    days_from    AS [From],
    days_to      AS [To],
    rows_written AS [Rows written],
    query_errors AS [Query errors],
    build_id     AS [Build],
    detail       AS [Detail]
FROM [${db}].dbo.gw_login_collector_run
WHERE project IN (${project:sqlstring})
ORDER BY started_at DESC;

list.definition: SELECT project FROM [${db}].dbo.gw_login_daily UNION SELECT project FROM [${db}].dbo.gw_login_collector_run ORDER BY project;
